projects.name: Backtesting lab
projects.label: Shelved
projects.what: Tools for testing trading strategies on historical data before risking any money.
detail: Four strategy families: momentum rotation, filtered dip-buying, a 200-day trend rule and a small-cap screener.
Walk-forward testing rebuilds the stock list using only data available at each point, so the test can’t peek ahead.
Parameter sweeps run over precomputed signals instead of recomputing each pass.

The chat agent has 27 tools, from logging a trade to importing broker history.
Scores out of 100 are weighted by what has worked for me before.

Built to run unattended through timeouts and failed polls.

projects.name: Atlas
projects.label: Live
projects.note: AI task automation, live at try-atlas.app. Public launch 27 Aug.
projects.when: 1 Apr – 9 Sep 2026, with commits on 109 days
projects.what: Type “every weekday at 8am, send me the top tech news” and Atlas runs it on that schedule, checks the answer, and sends you the result.
stack: or your own OpenAI or Anthropic key

facts.Built: 1 Apr – 9 Sep 2026, with commits on 109 days
facts.Code: ~140k lines of app code, ~212k lines of tests
facts.Built with: Node and Express, PostgreSQL, Clerk, Railway, Cloudflare, Brevo, LemonSqueezy. Gemini by default, or your own OpenAI or Anthropic key. Playwright and axe-core.

what_it_does: Reads the schedule straight out of the sentence. Nobody fills in a cron field.
Sends results by email or daily digest, Discord, Slack, Telegram or signed webhook, with Google Sheets and GitHub in beta.
Reply to a result email to change the task, with one-click undo.
Grades every run and warns you when a task has quietly stopped finding anything new.
Fetches live stock and crypto prices and headlines before the AI writes: about 230 company names map to tickers, and 37 coins are recognised.
Invite a friend and you both get 10 more runs.
how_its_built: One scheduler at a time. Postgres advisory locks keep scheduled jobs on a single leader, so a task never fires twice across instances.
Encrypted backups. Nightly database snapshots are AES-256-GCM encrypted and stored off-site, and a full restore has been checked end to end.
Stored credentials are encrypted at rest.
A launch gate that fails closed. The server alone decides whether the site is open, and a missing or malformed setting keeps it shut.
Answer quality. A classifier retries weak answers or switches provider, and an LLM-as-judge eval harness has run 52 times.
Release gate, 9 Sep: 456 unit test files and 596 Playwright tests passing, none flaky (from the project’s release record).

projects.name: Browser
projects.label: In use
projects.note: My own everyday browser, written in 6 days
projects.what: Claude coding sessions, Windows programs like Paint and Discord, and my Android phone all open as tabs beside ordinary web pages, in a browser I wrote.

facts.Code: ~63k lines of JavaScript, ~13k lines of CSS
facts.Built with: Electron, node-pty and xterm.js, koffi for Win32 calls, WebCodecs, scrcpy and adb, Ghostery ad blocker, Mozilla Readability
facts.Distribution: A Windows installer and a portable build (0.1.0, not code-signed)

what_it_does: Claude tabs: a real Claude Code session in each tab, with its own folder, resume, and a pulse when it needs me.
App tabs: real Windows programs hosted inside a tab, opened from a dock or by typing in the address bar.
Phone workspace: mirrors and fully controls my Android phone. The mouse acts as touch, and the clipboard works both ways.
Workspaces: the School workspace opens the right section of my class notes for the question on screen.
New tab page: clock, live CPU, memory, disk and network readouts, a process list and a Markets tile.
Ad blocking, reader view, split view, a command palette, tab sleep and picture-in-picture.
Phone sound plays on the computer, the phone or both, chosen from the phone rail.
how_its_built: Phone video decoded in the page with WebCodecs: about 59 fps at roughly 1 ms per frame. Painting from the decoder callback, instead of waiting for the next animation frame, stopped a quarter of frames from dropping.
Quality that adapts to a TCP round-trip probe, because timing adb itself costs about 170 ms even on a 7 ms link.
Windows apps hosted through Win32 SetParent via koffi, with no native rebuild. It passed 30 of 30 live checks with Paint.
CPU fixes, measured. The animated background went from 27% to 3% of a core, and stats sampling from 4.7% to 0.35%.
About 550 ms cold start. Hidden workspaces go to sleep, which fixed a 1.9 GB GPU process.
No silent failures. Every state shows its reason and what to do next.

projects.name: Family & staff portal
projects.label: Live
projects.note: Portal for a youth hockey academy
projects.what: A parent marks their skater absent for next Tuesday, a coach posts a video note on a skill, and the office imports its roster spreadsheet. All of it happens in one portal I built for a youth hockey academy.
stack: Vite and TypeScript with no framework

facts.Roles: Parents, students, staff and a maintainer
facts.Built with: Vite and TypeScript with no framework, Express, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Railway, Brevo, Cloudflare R2, GitHub Actions

what_it_does: Separate views for parents, students, staff and a maintainer.
Attendance with recurring absences and locked past dates, on one calendar with academy events.
Coach notes on skills, with video compressed in the browser before upload. Families can reply with a question.
Messages with read tracking, plus notifications and task lists.
Roster import from the office spreadsheet, and invite emails one at a time or all at once.
A draft board that splits the night’s skaters into two teams by drag and drop.
On-ice work: what each skater should be drilling, released to staff first.
how_its_built: Backups you can restore. Daily off-site backups alert if one fails or stops. A restore drill matched all 16 tables row for row, and the restore tool refuses to point at production.
Role boundaries under test. The tests run without a database and catch a deliberately planted cross-family leak.
Safe roster import. Preview and commit are separate endpoints, so a preview can never send an email. Invites are off by default, and every send asks first.
Migrations on every deploy, after the migration history was rebuilt from a clean baseline.
Email that lands. SPF and DKIM both pass, sent from a branded subdomain.
A maintainer console that logs failed sign-ins, dead reset links and server errors.
projects.admin_only_note: On-Ice Work shipped admin-only on 16 Sep 2026. Parent and student views exist in the release but families are not switched on.
